frequency_question: How often does institutional/structural friction successfully prevent the U.S. Education Department from finalizing a revocation of an accrediting agency's authority within a designated review window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal Department of Education initiation of action to limit, suspend, or terminate the recognition of an accrediting body. Excludes voluntary relinquishments or routine renewals without contested adverse proceedings.

cases.name: American College of Nurse-Midwives Division of Accreditation (2010)
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) First Action (2016)
American Bar Association initial deferral/compliance proceedings (2018)

coverage_note: 4 major contested agency recognition challenges identified in the modern regulatory era; universe is small due to the rarity of full termination attempts.
known_gaps: Lower-level compliance notices and informal corrective actions that never reached the formal revocation threshold are excluded.
skeleton: Total contested federal accreditation termination attempts since 1994 scaled by administrative success rate against procedural and statutory friction points.
multiplier: 4 attempted major review actions, resulting in 1 complete revocation blocked/delayed past standard windows and subsequent re-challenge, yielding a historical structural friction block rate of approximately 25 percent for final complete revocation prevention.
validity_reason: Administrative procedures governing the Department of Education recognition of accrediting agencies are anchored in long-standing federal regulations and statutory frameworks under the Higher Education Act, which change slowly.
